stem: Who is regarded as the “Mother of Indian Revolution”:
expl: Madam Cama was born on 24 September 1861. Her parents were Parsis. Sorabji Framji Patel was her father. She married Rustam K. R. Cama, who was a lawyer and a social worker. Madam Cama served as the private secretary to Dadabhai Naoroji, a great pioneer leader of India’s national movement. Later, after coming in contact with some patriotic students and European intellectuals, she joined the freedom movement. She participated in the International Socialist Conference held at Stuttgart, Germany, on 22 August 1907. In this very conference, she unfurled the Indian tricolour flag. She was the first person to hoist the Indian flag on foreign soil or on an international platform. The flag hoisted there was a modified form of the Calcutta Flag. She is called the ‘Mother of the Indian Revolution’.

stem: Ghadar Party was established in the year :
expl: In 1913, under the leadership of Sohan Singh Bhakna, an organization named the “Pacific Coast Hindustan Association” was established at Portland (Oregon), USA. Its headquarters were in San Francisco. This organization started publishing a newspaper named “Ghadar”, due to which the organization also came to be known as the Ghadar Party. Lala Har Dayal was the chief ideologue and guiding force of this organization. Its other members included—Ram Chandra, Barkatullah, Rash Behari Bose, Bhai Parmanand, etc.

stem: The person(s) associated with the 'Zimmermann Plan' was/were:
expl: During the First World War, Indian revolutionaries made a plan to procure arms and ammunition from Germany with the help of Indians living abroad. This came to be known as the “Hindu–German Conspiracy”, also referred to as the “Zimmermann Plan”. Lala Har Dayal, Bhupendranath Dutt, and Virendranath Chattopadhyay were connected with this plan. With German support, they established the “Berlin Committee / Berlin India Committee” in 1914. In 1915, this organization came to be known as the “Indian Independence Committee”.

stem: What was the cause of the outbreak of Ghadar Revolution –
expl: With the decline of the Swadeshi Movement, revolutionary activities also weakened for some time. Then, in 1914, the sudden outbreak of the First World War created a situation that the revolutionaries considered favourable for action. In North America, the Ghadar revolutionaries, and in India, leaders like Lokmanya Tilak and Annie Besant, and organizations like the Home Rule League tried to take advantage of this situation. The Ghadar revolutionaries attempted to overthrow British rule through armed struggle.
